newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-LIONS SHAKE OFF SLUGGISH START FOR EASY WIN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LIONS SHAKE OFF SLUGGISH START FOR EASY WIN.

text.p: Four tries inside the last quarter steadied the British Lions' opening match nerves and ensured a 39-11 victory over an Eastern Province Invitation XV on Saturday.

With 18 minutes remaining the Lions trailed 11-10 but touchdowns by lock Doddie Weir, substitute wing Tony Underwood, with his first touch, and centre Jeremy Guscott's second try paved the way to an ultimately comfortable win.
Centre Will Greenwood, the only uncapped player in the Lions' party, rounded off matters with his side's fifth try as the class in the visitors' back division stood out.
Neil Jenkins was also succesful with six out of eight kicks at goal, but it was the outstanding Guscott who put the Lions on track in the first-half with the tour's first try.
The England centre glided onto fly-half Gregor Townsend's slip pass to run untouched to the line.

Moving the ball at every opportunity the Lions looked capable of sweeping aside a home side which had been beefed up by the inclusion of Gauteng Lions Springboks in lock Kobus Wiese and centre Hennie le Roux as well as new signings -- former Australia back rower Sam Scott Young and New Zealand Barbarian Matthew Webber.
But a fifth new arrival, former Springbok full back Theo van Rensburg, kicked two of four first half penalties as the game settled down and the home side trailed only 10-6 at the interval.
A curving 40-metre run from right wing Deon Kayser sneaked them into the lead eight minutes after the restart and the Lions found themselves penned in their own half for extended periods.
But the complexion of the game was transformed when Weir was driven over by his tight forwards from close range to put the Lions back into the lead after 62 minutes.
Jenkins' conversion hit the post and bounced out -- as did his other failure from a penalty -- but he added a second penalty before the game was effectively ended with a dazzling run by Underwood.
He had been on the field for barely a minute when he picked up a loose ball 30 metres out and surged through a rooted defence to score by the posts.
Guscott crowned a dazzling personal performance with his second score two minutes later and Greenwood completed the job after Townsend and Underwood had combined to make the opening.

Eastern Province Invitiation XV: 15-Theo van Rensburg, 14-Deon Keyser, 13-Riaan van Jaarsveld, 12-Hennie le Roux, 11-Henry Pedro, 10-Ken Ford (Ronnie Fourie, 42), 9-Chad Alcock, 8-Jacques Greeff, 7-Sam Scott Young, 6-Matthew Webber, 5-Armand du Preez,4-Kobus Wiese, 3-Willie Enslin (Werner Lessing, 38), 2-Jaco Kirsten (captain), 1-Danie Saayman.

British Lions: 15-Neil Jenkins, 14-Ieuan Evans (Tony Underwood, 67), 13-Jeremy Guscott, 12-Will Greenwood, 11-Nick Beal, 10-Gregor Townsend, 9-Rob Howley, 8-Scott Quinnell, 7-Richard Hill, 6-Lawrence Dallaglio, 5-Simon Shaw (Jeremy Davidson, 77), 4-Doie Weir, 3-Jason Leonard (captain) 2-Keith Wood (Barry Wiliams 67), 1-Tom Smith.
